findings.problem: The email guarantees results ("We guarantee it removes 100% of the busywork"), which brand/voice.md forbids outright.
findings.fix: Remove the guarantee and state what we will actually do, e.g. "We take the repetitive production work off your team and hand back finished deliverables."

findings.problem: It claims "most agencies see a 40% revenue lift in the first month", an invented revenue number and promised lift that brand/voice.md never allows.
findings.fix: Delete the 40% lift claim and replace it with a concrete, provable statement about scope or process, with no numbers or implied outcomes.

findings.problem: A second link and second call to action ("See the detox plan") breaks the one-link rule in emails.md.
findings.fix: Delete line 9 so the email contains only the single scoping-call link.

findings.problem: The link text is "Claim your spot" instead of the required "Book a 30-minute scoping call", so it does not name the next step.
findings.fix: Change line 8 to exactly `[Book a 30-minute scoping call](https://zaeem-akhter.vercel.app)`.

findings.problem: The subject uses "Last chance" urgency hype and a vague "detox" label rather than saying what the work is, against the direct, practical voice.
findings.fix: Replace with a plain subject naming the offer, e.g. "Subject: Partner with us on AI delivery" (keep it within 50 characters including "Subject: ").
